English Gloss: Matrilineal clan / Extended family / Kinship unit
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The corporate matrilineal kin group; the fundamental ontological unit of identity, mutual insurance, and moral accountability in Akan society.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Abusua te sɛ kwaeɛ, wowɔ akyire a ɛyɛ kusuu, wokɔ mu a na wohunu sɛ dua biara si ne siberɛ.
Proverb Translation: The family is like a forest: from afar it looks dense and indivisible, but inside every tree stands in its own place.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Invoked to resolve internal disputes, demand mutual loyalty, and mandate funerary/crisis participation.

English Gloss: Mutual cooperative labor / Reciprocal farm assistance
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Traditional rotating communal labor system where community members cultivate each other's farms without wages, embodying relational mutualism.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Nsa baako nkura adesoa.
Proverb Translation: One hand alone cannot carry a heavy load.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Used to mobilize community members for communal projects, civic duties, or mutual aid.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The harmonious integration of disparate community members into an undivided collective whole; foundational to consensus democracy.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Nkabom mu na ahoɔden wɔ.
Proverb Translation: In unity lies indestructible collective strength.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Core rhetorical trope in chieftaincy arbitration, national solidarity appeals, and town councils.

English Gloss: Oneness / Collective solidarity / Acting in unison
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Unified collective agency prioritizing community well-being over sectional or egoistic interests.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Baanu so a, emmia.
Proverb Translation: When two people carry a heavy load together, it does not pinch or crush them.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Applied to encourage teamwork and eliminate interpersonal factionalism.

English Gloss: Every human is the sibling of human / Universal humanism
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The moral apex of Akan philosophy (Gyekye/Wiredu): every human possesses divine dignity (Okra) and is entitled to kinship obligations.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Onipa nua ne nipa; obi nnyaa ne yɔnko wɔ amanehunu mu.
Proverb Translation: A fellow human is one's sibling; no one should abandon their fellow traveler in distress.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Invoked as the highest moral argument for hospitality, stranger protection, and humanitarian assistance.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Spontaneous benevolence and deep visceral empathy toward community members in hardship.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ayamye nti na aboa adanko kɔe kɔtoo n'asaso mu.
Proverb Translation: It is out of pure benevolence that the hare gave up its shelter.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Pinnacle virtue expected of chiefs, wealthy benefactors, and community elders.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Active relational maintenance that weaves non-kin individuals into dependable social networks.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ayɔnkofa pa na ɛma abusua tim.
Proverb Translation: Enduring fellowship is what stabilizes the extended community.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Refers to steadfast, multi-generational familial and peer alliances.

English Gloss: Civic warrior group / Communal youth association
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Traditional civic and military organizations responsible for community defense, disaster management, and public works.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Asafo kɔ a, wɔkɔ biako.
Proverb Translation: When the communal company marches, it moves as a unified body.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Invoked during communal labor, civic emergencies, and traditional festivals.

English Gloss: The public / Humanity / The entire commonwealth
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The collective body of humanity or the nation, whose welfare supersedes any private ambition.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Amansan nyinaa yɛ Onyame mma.
Proverb Translation: All citizens of the commonwealth are the children of God.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Used in civic debates, royal declarations, and public service ethics.

English Gloss: Communal consultation / Deliberative caucus / Consensus council
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The formal caucus in Akan governance where leaders deliberate behind closed doors until unanimous consensus is achieved.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Agyinatuo mu na asɛm gye.
Proverb Translation: It is in collective deliberative caucus that difficult disputes are resolved.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Invoked in family inheritance meetings, court trials, and community arbitrations.

English Gloss: Selfishness / Greed / Solitary grasping / Extreme individualism
Morphology \/ Root: pɛ (want) + sɛ (that) + me (I) + nko (alone) + minya (I get)
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Pathologized individualism where personal accumulation occurs at the expense of communal welfare; viewed as moral decay.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Pɛsɛmenkominyafoɔ kɔ akuraa a, ɔno nko na ɔwe akokɔ.
Proverb Translation: When the selfish man goes to the village, he eats the whole chicken alone in isolation.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Severe social reproach applied to corrupt leaders, ungenerous kin, or resource hoarders.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Elevating oneself above others in defiance of social hierarchy, humility norms, and collective equality.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ahomasoɔ de brɛbrɛ kɔ owuo mu.
Proverb Translation: Arrogant self-exaltation marches steadily and inevitably toward ruin and death.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Warns individuals against boasting or displaying contempt toward elders or peers.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Flamboyant display of wealth or achievements that breaches communal egalitarian values and breeds resentment.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ahododoɔfoɔ tɔ nsuo mu a, obi nnye no.
Proverb Translation: When the boastful show-off falls into deep waters, onlookers hesitate to rescue him.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Used to counsel against conspicuous consumption and flashy boastfulness.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Excessive love and indulgence of one's own physical self and desires to the neglect of communal duties.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ahopɛ dodoɔ na ɛde ohia ba.
Proverb Translation: Excessive self-pampering and pleasure-seeking breeds poverty.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Used to caution against frivolous living and self-centered spending.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Disregarding collective advice or elder guidance in favor of stubborn self-determination.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Me ara me pɛ de onipa kɔ asɛm kɛseɛ mu.
Proverb Translation: Insisting on 'my own will alone' leads a person into catastrophe.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Applied to rebellious youth or stubborn adults who refuse familial mediation.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Insatiable lust for the possessions of others, undermining social trust and equity.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Anikonkrɔn de abususɛm ba.
Proverb Translation: Covetous greed breeds devastating internal strife within the clan.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Used in dispute resolutions involving theft, boundary disputes, or inheritance.

English Gloss: Jealousy / Malicious envy / Resentment of peer success
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Internal bitterness experienced when another community member prospers; seen as the root of witchcraft and spiritual malice.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ahoɔyaw de owuo ba.
Proverb Translation: Bitter envy breeds death and destruction.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Invoked to warn against competing with siblings or neighbors.

English Gloss: Greed for free goods / Gluttony / Parasitic grasping
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Craving to consume benefits of communal labor without contributing reciprocal effort.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Adifudepɛfoɔ kɔ afahyɛ a, ɔhwere n'animuonyam.
Proverb Translation: The parasitic glutton attends the festival and loses all his public dignity.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Used against opportunists who exploit communal hospitality.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Supreme Akan title of deference, uniting living monarchs, grandparents, and deified ancestors (Nsamanfoɔ) in a continuous cosmological chain.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Nana Nyame na ɔwɔ asase ne emu nnoɔma nyinaa.
Proverb Translation: Sovereign God possesses the earth and everything therein.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Mandatory address for chiefs, queenmothers, and biological/classificatory grandparents.

English Gloss: Elder / Moral arbiter / Person of maturity and wisdom
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: A status achieved through chronological maturity, ethical character, wisdom, and recognized arbitral capacity.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Opanyin nni fie a, mmofra didi abɔntene.
Proverb Translation: When the elder is absent from the home, children eat disorderly out in the open street.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Applied to heads of families, village elders, and respected arbiters.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The moral duty of acknowledging and yielding to age, rank, wisdom, and sacred authority.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Wobu opanyin a, wokora wo ankasa wo daakye so.
Proverb Translation: When you respect an elder, you safeguard your own future elderhood.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Fundamental prerequisite in the moral socialization of Akan children.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Voluntary restraint of ego to honor elders, superiors, and collective cohesion.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ahobraseɛ na ɛde animuonyam ba.
Proverb Translation: Humility is what ushers in enduring glory and social esteem.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Expected posture when appearing before chiefs, in-laws, or family councils.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Faithful, humble dedication to chiefs, elders, deities, and community institutions.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Wosom panin a, wonya panin adikan.
Proverb Translation: If you serve an elder with devotion, you earn the right to lead as an elder in turn.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Describes royal courtiers, religious acolytes, and apprentices.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The diplomatic bridge between ruler and people; filters raw speech into poetic, refined court language.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ɔhene nni aso; ɔkyeame na ɔte asɛm ma no.
Proverb Translation: The king has no direct public ears; the linguist listens and articulates on his behalf.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Direct unmediated address to a king is taboo; all dialogue must pass through the Okyeame.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The sacred custodian of the ancestral stool, embodying military, judicial, and spiritual leadership.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ɔhene nya ahotenafoɔ pa a, ne man gye mpuntuo.
Proverb Translation: When a king is surrounded by wise counselors, his nation flourishes.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Addressed with utmost ceremonial deference (*Nana Ohene*).

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The co-ruler and kingmaker who nominates the chief, arbitrates family and women's affairs, and serves as the ultimate moral compass.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ɔhemaa na ɔnim obi a ɔfata akonnwa no.
Proverb Translation: It is the queenmother who knows the legitimate heir worthy of the stool.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Possesses decisive veto power in royal succession disputes.

English Gloss: Solemn royal majesty / Grandeur / Court solemnity
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The intimidating grandeur and sacred aura surrounding the palace and the occupant of the Golden Stool.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ahemfie kuntunkruni ma obubuafoɔ mpo bɔ ne bra bɔkɔɔ.
Proverb Translation: The solemn grandeur of the royal palace makes even the boastful walk with reverence.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Describes the atmosphere during royal durbars and State festivals.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Kneeling before royalty or elders when making petitions, expressing repentance, or swearing allegiance.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Nkotodwe-gu na ɛtwe abufuo firi ɔpanyin bo.
Proverb Translation: Humble genuflection removes wrath from the heart of the elder.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Physical greeting etiquette required when approaching high chiefs.

Morphology \/ Root: akyi (back/turn away) + wa + deɛ (thing turned away from)
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Deed abhorred by deities, ancestors, and society; breaching it incurs severe cosmic pollution and social sanction.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Sɛ wodi akyiwadeɛ a, wobɔ wo nsam gu wo man so.
Proverb Translation: If you commit a taboo, you pour misfortune over your entire community.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Categorizes incest, suicide, insult to monarch, farming on sacred taboo days (e.g. Dabɔne).

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: A violation of cosmic order so severe that it threatens the collective existence unless ritually cleansed.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ɔbra bɔne de musuo ba fie.
Proverb Translation: Corrupt moral conduct brings spiritual abomination into the homestead.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Applied when crimes require ritual pacification and animal sacrifice (*Asubɔ*).

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The habituated moral nature of a person; the defining metric determining whether one is truly an 'onipa' (moral person).
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Suban pa na ɛkyɛn ahoɔfɛ.
Proverb Translation: Good moral character is far more precious than physical beauty.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Primary consideration in marriage proposals, chieftaincy enstoolment, and hiring.

English Gloss: Sacred taboo day / Non-working ritual day
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Specific days in the Akan 42-day calendar (Adae, Fofie, Awukudae) dedicated to ancestral communion where farming or tilling the earth is strictly forbidden.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Obi nkɔ asase so wɔ Dabɔne.
Proverb Translation: No one goes to till the sacred soil on a sacred taboo day.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Breaching Dabɔne farming taboos incurs heavy fines and sacrificial sheep penalties.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Sacred lustrations performed to cleanse people, royal stools, or land from moral and taboo contamination.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Asubɔ na ɛhohoro musuo gu.
Proverb Translation: Ritual purification is what washes away calamity and spiritual stain.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Central rite of the annual Odwira festival and post-taboo rehabilitation.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Hard-headed rebellion against elder counsel and established societal norms.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ti-ɛdenfoɔ kɔ asuo a, ɔde ahina bɔbo.
Proverb Translation: The stubborn person goes to the river and returns with a shattered clay pot.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Used in reprimanding deviant youth who disregard customary rules.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Literal 'hard-earedness'—refusal to listen to admonition, leading to social isolation and downfall.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Asoɔden de mmɔborɔhunu ba.
Proverb Translation: Disobedience inevitably yields misery and regret.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Standard descriptor for non-conformists and rule-breakers.

Morphology \/ Root: aso (ear) + twe (pulling / pulling by the ears)
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Formal disciplinary measures imposed by family heads or traditional courts to correct errant members.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Asotwe pa ma ɔba nya suban pa.
Proverb Translation: Righteous discipline gives a child good character.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Applied to customary fines, banishment, or physical discipline.

English Gloss: Reverence for God / Moral conscience rooted in Divine awe
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The interiorized moral fear of God's universal justice, serving as an omnipresent internal inhibitor against secret sins.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Nyamesuro ne nyansa nyinaa mfitiaseɛ.
Proverb Translation: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of all true wisdom.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Considered the ultimate foundation of trustworthy character (*Onipa a ɔwɔ Nyamesuro*).

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Invocation of a tragic historical calamity of a royal lineage; serves as an immediate injunction halting dispute actions until court review.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Woka ntan a, wodi ho adanseɛ wɔ badwa mu.
Proverb Translation: When you swear an oath, you must bear testimony and abide by the judgment of the assembly.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Customary legal injunction (e.g. *Ntamkɛseɛ* - The Great Oath of Asante).

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Literal 'brightness of the face'; the spiritual and moral charisma radiating from integrity, ancestral favor, and community respect.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Dintiti pa kyɛn ahonyadeɛ.
Proverb Translation: A good, untarnished name is greater than vast material fortunes.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Bestowed upon leaders, virtuous citizens, and benefactors.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The deep psychological aversion to public disgrace; acts as the internal regulatory conscience preventing unethical behavior.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Fɛre nni aduro.
Proverb Translation: There is no medicinal herb that can wipe away the stain of public shame.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Communal mechanism for self-policing without external police presence.

English Gloss: Disgrace / Public humiliation / Contempt / Diminishing face
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Diminishing someone's public dignity through disrespect or exposure of fault.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Mma obiara mmɔ wo animtia wɔ bagua mu.
Proverb Translation: Do not invite public humiliation upon yourself before the gathered council.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Used when reprimanding public insults, mocking elders, or slander.

English Gloss: Ignominy / Total social disgrace / Ruin of face
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Total loss of honor and moral standing in the public sphere, bringing shame to the entire clan (*Abusua*).
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Owuo pa sen anim-guaseɛ.
Proverb Translation: An honorable death is far preferable to living in public disgrace.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Core Akan honor code motto expressing that physical death is superior to dishonor.

English Gloss: Spotless reputation / Great name / Enduring integrity
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: A sterling moral reputation accumulated over generations that provides social capital and blessing to one's descendants.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Din pa na ɛdi bem wɔ ahemfie.
Proverb Translation: A good name is acquitted without difficulty in the royal palace.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Invoked to discourage shady shortcuts to wealth.

Morphology \/ Root: ani (eye/presence) + da-ho (lying in place / remaining steady)
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Maintaining calm, dignified poise in the face of provocation or difficulty without losing self-control.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Anidaho ma onipa kɔ so di panyin.
Proverb Translation: Dignified self-restraint maintains a person's standing as a mature elder.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Expected of judges, spokespersons, and parents.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Artfully indirect language used to convey hard truths without causing offense or breaching status hierarchy.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ɔpanyin kasa a, ɔka no kasakoa mu na amaneɛ ansɛe.
Proverb Translation: When an elder speaks, he uses subtle nuance and circumlocution to preserve harmony.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Vital in diplomatic missions, marriage negotiations, and royal discourse.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The condensed distillation of historical and moral wisdom; used as indirect rhetorical tools to persuade, reprimand, and resolve conflicts.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ɔbadwemma na wɔbɔ no bɛ, na wɔnnkã asɛm mprɔprɔ nnkyerɛ no.
Proverb Translation: A wise child is addressed in proverbs, not through raw, blunt speech.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Required element of eloquent Akan public address (*Kasa pa*).

English Gloss: Gentle speech / Soft, tempered speech / Diplomatic tone
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Speech delivered with calmness and tact to pacify anger and prevent rupture in social ties.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Kasa bɔkɔɔ dwudwo abufuo ano.
Proverb Translation: Soft and gentle speech cools the fiercest wrath.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Counsel given to disputants during arbitration.

English Gloss: Raw speech / Blunt aggressive speech / Uncouth language
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Speaking bluntly without diplomatic framing or proverbial cushion; considered immature and offensive in Akan oratorical ethics.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Kasa-mprɔprɔ de ntɔkwa ba badwa mu.
Proverb Translation: Blunt, unfiltered speech causes brawls in the assembly.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Severely reprimanded in courtroom proceedings and marriage mediation.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: A carefully weighed, pregnant sentence whose brevity conveys vast contextual weight and authority.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Ɔpanin kasafua baako pɛ gye ɔman.
Proverb Translation: A single weighed word from an elder can save an entire nation.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Used when an elder settles a protracted dispute with a concise, decisive verdict.

English Gloss: Consulting an elder / Seeking seasoned counsel
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The mandatory cultural protocol of seeking elder verification before initiating marriage, land purchase, or public statements.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Wobisa panyin a, womfom kwan.
Proverb Translation: If you inquire of the elder, you never lose your pathway.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Pre-condition in Akan customary transactional law.

English Gloss: Divine Soul / Inner destiny / Spark of Supreme Being
Morphology \/ Root: kra (to bid farewell / to receive divine mandate from Nyame)
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The divine essence bestowed directly by Onyame; carries an individual's pre-destined fate (Nkrabea) and intrinsic human dignity.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Obi nkra Nyame na ɔnkyerɛ no.
Proverb Translation: No one teaches another how to receive destiny from God; every soul is independently accountable to God.
Pragmatic Usage Note: The source of unconditional moral worth in Akan humanism.

Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The experiential, moral, and dynamic spirit inherited from the father (Ntɔro); determines one's psychological strength and moral character.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Sunsum duru na ɛtumi fa asɛm ho.
Proverb Translation: A weighty, formidable spirit is what withstands adversity and witchcraft.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Used in evaluating charismatic leadership (*Sunsum kɛseɛ* / *Sunsum duru*).

English Gloss: Blood / Maternal biological essence / Clan foundation
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The physical substance transmitted solely by mothers that forms the biological basis of the *Abusua* (clan) and citizenship.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Mogya yɛ duru sen nsuo.
Proverb Translation: Blood is thicker than water.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Legal determinant of Akan inheritance and royal stool succession.

English Gloss: Paternal spirit group / Patrilineal moral archetype
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: The spiritual grouping passed from father to child, determining moral temperament, taboo observances (Akyiwadeɛ), and greeting responses (*Yaa Agya*, *Yaa Asɔn*).
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Agya ntɔro na ɛbɔ ɔba ho ban.
Proverb Translation: The father's spirit provides spiritual protection for the child.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Determines daily conversational greeting etiquette across Akan subgroups.

English Gloss: Ancestors / The living-dead / Guardians of morality
Cultural & Philosophical Definition: Departed elders who lived virtuous lives, now existing as spiritual intermediaries and enforcers of custom, law, and morality.
Sample Proverb \/ Expression (Ɛbɛ): Nsamanfoɔ ani da hɔ; wɔhunu adeɛ nyinaa.
Proverb Translation: The ancestors are ever watchful; they perceive all secret actions.
Pragmatic Usage Note: Libations (*Nsaguo*) are poured to them at every public state or family ceremony.
